Report: /home/user/m/apex/research/experiments/E1_forecast_paths.md (sections 1-13). Section 1, the pre-registration from the interrupted attempt, is byte-for-byte unchanged (SHA-256 fd1e5609...a31, checked after every edit). Code is in /home/user/m/apex/validation/python/experiments/E1_forecast_paths/. Outputs (results.json, tables.md, summary.md, bands_posthoc.json) are in its out/ folder, which is git-ignored. Nothing was committed.

RESUME AUDIT. The earlier attempt left:
- the pre-registration, written 09:50 UTC on 2026-11-27, before the first forecast output at 09:55;
- a complete e1_run.py and its forecast files;
- an e1_eval.py that died in its first stage.

I checked the inherited work instead of trusting it (e1_verify.py):
- Timestamps are UTC: the missing hour is 22:00 UTC in January and 21:00 UTC in July, which is 17:00 New York in both.
- GC 1h is corrupted: 289 jump-and-back bars, median volume 4 against 257 overall, so it stays excluded. The GC 1-minute file is clean (0 jump-and-back), so GC 5m is kept.
- CL 1h has 17 jump-and-back bars. They are high-volume March-April 2026 shock bars and are kept.
- Feature truncation tests (NQ 1h, NQ 5m, BTC 1h): features computed on data[:N] equal the full-data features at every bar < N.
- Fit truncation tests (NQ 1h, ES 5m): walk-forward parameters fitted at refit T are identical whether the data ends at T or later.

I then reran the forecasts and the full evaluation in a new venv built from the local wheels (numpy 2.5.5, pandas 3.1.1, scipy 1.18.1). The data-lab loader apexdata.py did not exist, so the raw CME and BTC files were loaded directly.

DESIGN (pre-registered):
- 12 series: NQ, ES, YM, RTY, CL and GC at 5m; NQ, ES, YM, RTY and CL at 1h; BTC at 1h. There is no BTC 5m file.
- Expanding walk-forward with refits every R bars and a 121-bar purge. The headline is the chronological second half (the holdout).
- Methods: zero-drift RW baseline; historical drift; OLS drift over 50, 100 and 200 bars, plus a line-end variant; engine-style momentum (c0); momentum with an online fitted decay (c); volatility-scaled drift with sqrt-time and a time-of-day clock (d); state drift by structure bias × volatility tercile (e); a target bridge to the nearest liquidity level, weighted by the past reach rate (f); and a shrinkage blend (g).
- Metrics: MAE and RMSE in ATR units vs the RW, with HAC/HLN Diebold-Mariano tests, Holm/BH corrections and block-bootstrap CIs; directional accuracy (Wilson on non-overlapping origins, compared with 50% and with always-up); path-shape MAE; residual quantile bands with coverage by horizon and volatility tercile; an after-cost economic check with the Deflated Sharpe Ratio.

RESULTS:
- No method beats the random walk: 0 of 99 tests pass.
- On MAE no test reaches even a nominal p < 0.05 before correction. The best is 0.997 for c on CME 1h at H = 60 (p = 0.28, CI [0.987, 1.007]).
- Methods that make the path worse:
  - regression extrapolation: 7-118% worse;
  - engine-style momentum: 6.5-23% worse;
  - target bridge toward the DOL level: 2.3-6.7% worse, with all 9 pool × horizon CIs excluding 1 on the worse side;
  - state drift: 0.6-4.8% worse out of sample, after looking 6.1% better in-sample.
- The shrinkage blend collapses toward zero drift, as designed.
- The only nominal secondary wins are g's RMSE on BTC: 0.996-0.999, p 0.02-0.05, Holm ≥ 0.67. That is negligible.
- Direction shows no edge: accuracy at H = 60 is 0.41-0.55, and no method beats always-up.
- Path-shape error: the best ratio is 1.000-1.002.
- Economics: 3 of 99 trials have a CI above 0, which chance alone produces; the maximum DSR is 0.555.

BANDS:
- Unconditional bands are wrongly sized by volatility regime: coverage is 0.63-0.73 in low volatility and 0.85-0.89 in high volatility.
- Conditioning on the volatility tercile (U3) fixes this and passes the calibration criterion on CME 5m and CME 1h. It fails on BTC at k = 120 (coverage 0.744).
- The time-of-day clock version (U2) passes on CME 5m and BTC and fails on CME 1h.
- Gaussian ±1.28σ (U4) passes on BTC only and over-covers CME by up to 8 pp. Plain ATR·√k bands (U1) fail everywhere.
- A post-hoc, exploratory run shows that coverage depends on c = W/k, the number of independent horizons in the window: c = 5 gives 0.68-0.79, and c ≥ 25 gives 0.776-0.799.

RECOMMENDATION: present the one forward path as a scenario cone. The centre line is zero drift (flat at the close); the 10-90% band comes from tercile-conditioned empirical residual quantiles; the colour comes from the structure bias; the DOL target is a separately labelled scenario; and bands are shown only when the history holds enough independent horizons.
result.summary:
I finished the interrupted assignment: I audited the draft, ran lookahead truncation tests and reran everything. The result is a clean null: no forward-path method beats a zero-drift random walk out of sample.
- 0 of 99 pre-registered tests pass, across 12 series (CME at 5m and 1h, BTC at 1h) and horizons of 20, 60 and 120 bars.
- On MAE, no test reaches a nominal p < 0.05; the best ratio is 0.997 (p = 0.28).
- Methods that make the path significantly worse: regression extrapolation (7-118%), engine-style momentum (6-23%) and the target bridge toward the DOL level (2-7%, all 9 CIs exclude 1). State drift overfits: it looks 6% better in-sample and is 2% worse on the holdout.
- No directional edge, no better path shape, and no after-cost edge (maximum DSR 0.555).
- What can be estimated honestly is uncertainty. Tercile-conditioned empirical residual quantiles calibrate on CME 5m and CME 1h and fail on BTC at k = 120. Post-hoc, the window needs at least about 25 independent horizons (W ≥ 25·H) for coverage within 2-3 pp of nominal.
- Recommendation: draw a zero-drift scenario cone coloured by the bias, show the DOL target as a separately labelled scenario, and add a live coverage self-check.

findings.hypothesis: Rolling linear-regression drift extrapolation (b50/b100/b200/bL100) beats the zero-drift RW on holdout MAE at t+H
findings.result: Worse than the RW in every pool, horizon and symbol (0 of 12 symbols below 1 in any cell). It gets worse with a longer H and a shorter window.
findings.n: Holdout origins: CME 5m 42,459; CME 1h 10,751; BTC 37,969 (≈700 / 180 / 630 independent 60-bar windows)

findings.hypothesis: Momentum persistence beats the RW: c0, the engine-style EMA momentum with a fixed decay, and c, the online-fitted decay
findings.result: c0 is significantly worse everywhere. c is indistinguishable from the RW, and its fitted coefficient flips sign by instrument and timeframe (negative at 1h for NQ and ES, positive for BTC).
findings.n: Same holdout origins as F1; 33 tests per pool

findings.hypothesis: Volatility-scaled drift with sqrt-time scaling and a time-of-day volatility clock (d) beats the RW
findings.result: Indistinguishable from the RW. Its kappa changes sign by instrument (CL 1h -0.34, BTC +0.17, NQ 5m -0.06).
findings.effect: H=60 MAE ratio 1.006 (CME 5m), 0.999 (CME 1h), 1.008 (BTC); all Holm p = 1

findings.hypothesis: State-dependent drift (structure bias × volatility tercile, mean forward return from past data) beats the RW
findings.result: Worse out of sample in every pool and horizon. It is a clear overfit: in-sample it looks 6.1% better on CME 1h at H=60.
findings.n: Same holdout origins as F1; a state needs ≥300 training origins
findings.effect: OOS MAE ratio 1.006-1.048. CME 1h H=60: IS 0.939 vs holdout 1.021

findings.hypothesis: Target-aware shaping (a bridge toward the nearest PDH/PDL or confirmed swing on the bias side, weighted by the past reach rate) beats the RW
findings.result: Significantly worse in all 9 pool × horizon cells. Never better than the RW in any symbol.
findings.n: Same holdout origins as F1; target found at 91-98% of origins
findings.ci: CME 1h H=60 [1.033, 1.104]; BTC H=20 [1.034, 1.050]; every CI excludes 1 on the worse side

findings.hypothesis: A shrinkage blend of the components toward zero drift (g) beats the RW
findings.result: It collapses to zero drift; many blocks have all weights at 0. On MAE it equals the RW. On BTC there is a faint RMSE gain that does not survive correction and is negligible in size.

findings.hypothesis: Some forecast method shows directional accuracy at H above 50% and above an always-up baseline (Wilson lower bound > 50% per symbol; bootstrap CI vs always-up excludes 0)
findings.result: No method passes. On CME 1h several are significantly worse than always-up (b50 -0.126, f -0.110, c0 -0.081). Only 2 per-symbol Wilson lower bounds exceed 50%, which is chance level, and neither beats always-up consistently.
findings.n: Non-overlapping origins per symbol at H=60: about 122 (5m), 39 (CME 1h; 24 for CL), 633 (BTC)
findings.effect: H=60 pooled accuracy: CME 5m 0.482-0.513 (always-up 0.502); CME 1h 0.411-0.554 (always-up 0.537); BTC 0.497-0.529 (always-up 0.529)

findings.hypothesis: Some method has a lower path-shape error (MAE over steps 1..H) than the flat RW path
findings.result: None does. The b family is 5-84% worse along the path, c0 11-21% and f 4-8%.
findings.effect: Best path-MAE ratio 1.000-1.002 in every pool and horizon; smallest raw p 0.29; every Holm p = 1

findings.hypothesis: Trading in the forecast direction (enter at the next open, exit after H bars, non-overlapping) has positive expectancy after costs
findings.result: 3 of 99 trials have a CI lower bound above 0, roughly the 2.5 expected by chance. None survives deflation. Round-trip costs are only 0.01-0.15 ATR against a typical move of 2.6-7.9 ATR, so costs are not what blocks an edge.
findings.n: 99 trials; e.g. CME 1h H=60 has 180 trades, BTC H=60 has 633
findings.effect: Best: CME 1h H=60 c +1.52 ATR/trade (DSR 0.555); BTC H=120 a2 +1.37 (DSR 0.296); BTC H=60 e +0.58 (DSR 0.210)

findings.hypothesis: Volatility-clock bands (U2) calibrate better than ATR·sqrt(k) bands (U1): 80% coverage within ±5 pp at every k and ±8 pp in every volatility tercile
findings.result: U1 fails in every pool. U2 passes on CME 5m and BTC but fails on CME 1h. The clock is not uniformly better.
findings.n: Holdout band origins: CME 5m 42,459; CME 1h ~10,082; BTC 37,969 (W=2000)
findings.effect: U2 coverage at k=20/60/120: CME 5m 0.822/0.794/0.779; CME 1h 0.746/0.768/0.813 (tercile spread 11.8 pp); BTC 0.800/0.783/0.759. U1: worst tercile deviation 15-16 pp

findings.hypothesis: Empirical per-horizon residual quantile bands conditioned on the volatility tercile (U3) are calibrated, and unconditional bands (U0) are not
findings.result: U0 fails everywhere: it is too narrow in low volatility and too wide in high volatility. U3 passes on CME 5m and CME 1h. It fails on BTC at k=120 because its per-tercile window (667) holds only about 5.6 independent 120-bar horizons.
findings.effect: U0 k=60 tercile coverage: 0.63-0.73 low vol, 0.85-0.89 high vol. U3 k=60 tercile spread 1-6 pp; U3 coverage at k=120: 0.757 / 0.794 / 0.744 (CME 5m / CME 1h / BTC)

findings.hypothesis: POST-HOC, exploratory: band coverage depends on the number of independent horizons in the window, c = W/k, not on W itself
findings.result: Coverage rises with c. At c ≥ 25 it is within about 2-3 pp of 80%, with a persistent 1-2 pp shortfall at k=120. Conditioning on the tercile keeps the terciles balanced; unconditional bands do not. This reuses an already-seen holdout.
findings.n: 108 cells (2 schemes × 6 c × 3 k × 3 pools), RW centre, holdout
findings.ci: n/a (descriptive coverage rates over ~10k-42k origins per cell)

designImplications: Default central path: zero drift, a flat median at the last close. No candidate beat it. The shrinkage blend converges to it anyway, and spec §25 says to prefer the simpler model. Do NOT ship regression-line extension, the fixed-decay EMA momentum projection (the current engine style), a path bent toward the DOL target, or state-mean drift. Each made the path measurably worse out of sample.

Present the 'one forward path' (spec §14) as a scenario cone. The centre line is the band median (≈ the last close). The q10-q90 cone is drawn for k=1..H and coloured green or red by the structure/DOL bias state. Label it, e.g. 'Bias: bullish (structure) · drift forecast: none detected · 80% range'. At H=60 the cone spans about 14-16 ATR, so it is large and visible without inventing drift.

Draw the DOL target only as a separately labelled conditional scenario ('if bias holds -> target'), never as the expected path. Optionally state the target's end-of-horizon quantile inside the cone. A touch or reach probability must come from a separately calibrated model (spec §15).

Uncertainty method (default U3). At anchor horizons, store the realized z = (C[s+j] - C[s]) / ATR14[s], added only once realized (s + j <= t). Tag each with the volatility tercile at origin s: the percentile rank of ATR14/close over the trailing 500 bars, with cuts at 1/3 and 2/3. Band(k) = C_t + ATR14_t × quantile_{0.10, 0.50, 0.90}(z_k | current tercile). Default per-tercile window W_g = 33·H realized origins (1,980 for H=60). Use ring buffers and array.percentile_linear_interpolation, evaluated on the last bar only. Interpolating linearly in sqrt(k) between anchors (e.g. H/6 ... H) for a continuous cone is NOT RUN and needs checking.

Fallback when the per-tercile history is too short: unconditional per-horizon quantiles (U0, W = 33·H), labelled 'not regime-adjusted' (at W=2000 its coverage is 2-18 pp too low in low volatility and 4-9 pp too high in high volatility). Do not use Gaussian ±1.28σ or plain ATR·sqrt(k) bands as the default. The time-of-day clock is an optional refinement only: it fails on CME 1h and needs a learned slot table.

Minimum sample before bands are shown, counted as independent horizons n_eff = W/H in the current tercile (post-hoc evidence). n_eff >= 25: show the cone normally (H=60 needs about 1,500 realized origins per tercile, roughly 4,500 + 500 + H bars; H=120 needs about 9,000+ bars). 10 <= n_eff < 25: dashed and labelled 'provisional' (expected coverage about 0.74-0.80). n_eff < 10: no band, show only a 'not enough history for a range' note (coverage 0.68-0.79, typically 0.70-0.75).

Horizon: keep 60 as the default; drift is equally absent at 20, 60 and 120. Expect H=120 cones to run about 1-2 pp narrow even with long history. Either label it '≈78% at the longest horizon' or apply a small documented widening after live validation.

Add a live self-check ledger of past cones that displays realized coverage, e.g. 'last 200 cones: 77% inside the 80% band'. Build the Forecast Quality Score (spec §13 F) from n_eff and this live coverage, not from directional agreement, because no directional skill at H was detected.
Never attach a probability or accuracy figure to the path's direction. The measured direction-at-H accuracy is 50% ± noise. A bias colour describes structure; it does not forecast the next H bars.

Promotion rule: a future drift component (from E3, E7, E9 or others) may replace zero drift only if it passes section 1.5 on this harness: Holm-corrected pooled DM on the holdout, a majority of symbols better, the same sign in WF-dev, and at least a 2% MAE gain to be called meaningful.
caveats: Short CME history. The 5m data spans about 12 weeks; its holdout is about 5.5 weeks (2026-03-09 to 2026-04-15) and includes the March 2026 oil shock. The 1h data spans about 13 months (CL from 2025-06). BTC spans 9 years but is a single asset. Each instrument has one chronological holdout, so the result belongs to one regime per instrument.
GC 1h was excluded, not repaired (two contract months interleaved). GC is evaluated at 5m only, from the clean 1-minute file. There is no BTC 5m data.
The roll construction of the continuous futures in the source clone is undocumented. Roll jumps, if present, are dampened by ATR normalization but not removed.
The DM test with Bartlett HAC at lag H only approximates the variance for overlapping forecasts and can be slightly anti-conservative. It does not matter here: no MAE test comes near significance.

Structure and target parameters were fixed (pivot length 5, the target candidate set, the distance buckets). Other definitions could behave differently, although every method family failed in the same direction.

The band-window rule (n_eff >= 25) and the strength of the U3 recommendation rest partly on post-hoc analysis (108 cells) of an already-seen holdout. Confirm them with APEX's live coverage self-check and in the Phase-6 validation.

Minor disclosed deviations, none changing a conclusion: (1) for CME 1h, the active-slot calendar used by method d and the U2/U4 bands came from the first 2000 bars while T0 = 1500 (presence of bars only, no prices; WF-dev only); (2) the f and g paths at the U1/U2 pooling horizons came from the smallest containing H; (3) U3 used W/3 per tercile.
The data-lab loader (apexdata.py) and catalog did not exist at run time, so the raw files were loaded directly.
NOT RUN: interpolation of the cone between anchor horizons; a cross-check of a Pine implementation against this Python reference; GC 1h repair.
